e-6254.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A),$ we need reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -4 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2.$ So, a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is $\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 \},$ that is to say,

a

b

EXPLANATION

In order to find a basis of Col(F), we reduce the matrix F to row echelon form:

F=[−137−2]R2:=R2+7R1∼[−13019]

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the 1st and 2nd columns are pivot columns.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the original matrix, not from the reduced one.

The 1st and 2rd columns from the original matrix are f1 and f2. So, a basis of Col(F) is {f1,f2}, that is to say,

B={[−17],[3−2]}.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix
content.problem:
Given the matrix 
$F=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(F).$
content.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(F),$ we reduce the matrix $F$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 7 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 0 & 19\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$rd columns from the original matrix are ${f}_{1}$ and ${f}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(F)$ is ${{f}_{1},{f}_{2}},$ that is to say, 

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}.
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given the matrix 
$F=[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 12 & 4\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(F).$
after.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(F),$ we reduce the matrix $F$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 12 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st and $2$nd columns are pivot columns, while the $3$rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st and $2$nd columns from the original matrix are ${f}_{1}$ and ${f}_{2}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(V)$ is ${{f}_{1},{f}_{2}},$ that is to say, 

$$

EXPLANATION

In order to find a basis of Col(F), we reduce the matrix F to row echelon form:

F=[1620−302124]R3:=R3+(−2)R1∼[1620−30000]

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the 1st and 2nd columns are pivot columns, while the 3rd column is a non-pivot column.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the original matrix, not from the reduced one.

The 1st and 2nd columns from the original matrix are f1 and f2. So, a basis of Col(V) is {f1,f2}, that is to say,

B={[102],[6−312]}.
